description: Shared filesystem-jail vectors for the Python (agent_tool_sandbox.boundary) and TS (src/fs-jail.ts) packages. Each vector builds a layout in a fresh temp directory ({base}), runs one operation and records each language's observed verdict. Harnesses: python/tests/test_shared_fs_vectors.py and ts/test/shared-fs-vectors.test.ts.
notes: op 'boundary': assert_inside_boundary(input, root, deny_roots) / assertInsideBoundary(input, root, {denyRoots}). allow = the resolved path (base-relative).

op 'read': Python assert_no_symlink(root / input, operation='read'), assert_inside_boundary, os.open(O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW) and read; TS readFileJailed. allow = the bytes of the resolved file were returned.

op 'write': Python assert_no_symlink(root / input), assert_inside_boundary, mkdir(parents=True) and write_text; TS writeFileJailed(..., {createParents: true}). allow = the data landed at the resolved path. For every write vector nothing outside the root may change; for a deny nothing at all may change.

Python reasons are mapped from the ValueError message: 'Dotfile rejected' DOTFILE, 'Path traversal rejected' TRAVERSAL, 'Denied root' DENIED_ROOT, 'Symlink rejected on' SYMLINK, 'Symlink in path rejected on' SYMLINK_IN_PATH, 'Path not inspectable on' UNINSPECTABLE, 'embedded null' (os.lstat's NUL ValueError, worded per version) INVALID_PATH. Any other exception fails the test.
Placeholders: {base} is the temp directory (realpath'd), {root} is {base}/<root>. Layout paths, root and deny_roots are base-relative.
expected.python and expected.ts are observed behaviour. They must be equal unless the vector has a 'divergence' string, and must differ if it has one.

Not in this corpus: uninspectable paths (EACCES). chmod 000 gives EACCES only without CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE (not as root, not as uid 0 of the offline.sh user namespace), and CPython 3.13+ Path.is_symlink() returns False on EACCES, so Python's assert_no_symlink does not fail closed there (its test simulates 3.12 by patching). TS fails closed on every lstat error except ENOENT/ENOTDIR/ELOOP/EBADF; see ts/test/fs-jail.test.ts and ts/test/fs-jail-races.test.ts.
No layout entry may be named .env*; '.env' spellings are inputs only, refused before any open.

vectors.divergence: Both refuse. Python's assert_no_symlink lets a NUL path through (Path.is_symlink() returns False on ValueError), so the dotfile rule in assert_inside_boundary names the refusal; TS's assertNoSymlink fails closed on the NUL first. Only the reason differs.
